summary: Progressive, largely irreversible airflow limitation from chronic airway/alveolar inflammation; diagnosis requires postbronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.70. Overwhelmingly smoking-related, rising sharply with age (US age-adjusted prevalence 3.8% of adults 18+, 10.5% at 75+); 5th-leading US cause of death in 2023 (141,733 deaths). Presents as chronic dyspnea, cough, and sputum production punctuated by exacerbations. GOLD 2026 reframes management around "disease activity" (ongoing inflammation, symptom variability, exacerbation risk) layered on ABE risk groups, pairing stepped inhaled bronchodilator +/- ICS therapy with smoking cessation, vaccination, and pulmonary rehabilitation.

news.what: GOLD 2026 Report (v1.3; pocket guide v1.1, 2025-11-20) released, superseding GOLD 2024/2025: reframes COPD around disease activity; escalate therapy after even one moderate exacerbation (prior reports used 2+/yr); RSV vaccination now recommended for adults 50 and over; GOLD does not recommend population-wide spirometry screening. Publication date is ambiguous across sources (one gives 2025-11-10).

FDA approved Dupixent (dupilumab), first biologic for COPD, add-on for an eosinophilic phenotype (blood eosinophils >=300/uL in pivotal trials), on BOREAS/NOTUS (30-34% exacerbation-rate reduction). Outside the usual 18-month window; carried as the only approved COPD biologic.
FDA approved Ohtuvayre (ensifentrine), first new inhaled COPD mechanism in over 20 years, on ENHANCE-1/ENHANCE-2. Outside the usual 18-month window; carried as the newest inhaled mechanism.
Context: COPD age-adjusted prevalence 3.8% of US adults 18+, rising to 10.5% at 75+; data year 2023, published May 2025.
